scope: Power map of India's coal sector: Ministry of Coal ministers 2014–2026, Coal India and subsidiaries, NLC India, Singareni, CMPDI; the commercial-auction regime 2020–26 (rounds, single-bid allocations, top winners); MDO contracts held by Adani Enterprises and Essel Mining for state gencos and NLC; the PEKB/Hasdeo Arand chain (RRVUNL–PKCL–Adani, 2011 and 2022 clearances, 2025 Jaipur court finding); the DRI/FT coal-import over-invoicing controversy and denials; Section 11/blending mandates 2021–24 and NTPC/CIL import tenders; electoral-bond purchases by coal-sector companies; and two opposition-side controls (Chhattisgarh coal levy, West Bengal ECL coal theft). It deliberately leaves out: the block-by-block auction spine (already in research/raw/resources-coal.json), the pre-2014 Screening Committee era, coking-coal imports, captive-block end-use compliance, and CIL/subsidiary annual-report CSR annexures (not reachable this pass — recorded as the principal gap).

symmetryCheck: Control 1 — Odisha under BJD (not BJP): the same lens (mining companies → ruling party via bonds, MDO/lease dependence on the state) produces an equally dense picture: Essel Mining Rs 174.5 cr, JSPL Rs 100 cr, Rungta Sons Rs 50 cr, Vedanta Rs 40 cr, Utkal Alumina Rs 70 cr to BJD (Rs 775.5 cr from 42 donors, mostly mining/metals). Control 2 — Congress-run Chhattisgarh 2018–23: an ED case alleging a Rs 540 cr coal levy run from the CMO with a former minister and an MLA among 35 accused, untried. Control 3 — TMC-run West Bengal: a CBI/ED coal-theft case (Rs 1,352 cr) in which the ruling party's general secretary is a summonee. Control 4 — Hasdeo: the two clearances that opened Adani-operated mining (2011 MoEF; 2022 Chhattisgarh) were given by Congress ministers/governments, and the MDO contract was signed under a BJP Rajasthan government in 2008 — the chain crosses party lines at every link. Conclusion: the 'donor wins coal' lens generates alarming graphs for every party that controls coal-bearing territory; it detects proximity to the state, not a BJP-specific mechanism. What remains discriminating and party-specific after the control: (a) the DRI/FT import over-invoicing question, which concerns a private group's pricing rather than any party; (b) the Union-level blending mandate that routed ~Rs 16,700 cr of NTPC import contracts to one supplier in 2022, where the rival record (CIL chose an Indonesian supplier over Adani) cuts against a capture story.
